4. Hence he has filed application challenging the legality and propriety of Respondent No. 3 lease out their inherited property in favour of others considering it as a Government Khas land. 

 7. Mr Mustafa Niaz Mahammad with Mr Md Belal Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the predecessor of the present petitioners purchased the land in question from one Salimullah son of late Mokrom Ali in the year 1978 by virtue of Kabala Annexure-B to the petition and since then they have been possessing the same peacefully; as such respondent Nos. 1-3 have or had no right to declare it alluvial Khas land of the Government gradually raised by accretion from the Bay of Bengal; but in support of their private ownerships they have produced not a single piece of document to show how their predecessor-in-interest acquired his title in the land in the year 1978 which usually remains under water of Bay of Bengal at time of high tide. 

 10. The above identification, made by the respondent No. 3 clearly stands to say that this is not virtually any and rather it is sea bed where sea water comes in regularly at the time of high tide. So certainly it cannot be considered as alluvial land though no such declaration has yet been made in accordance with law. The learned Deputy Attorney General further goes to argue that whenever any land is accreted from the course of any river or sea it will be treated as khas land and respondent No. 1 is authorized to lease out the same for the purpose of collection of revenue of the Government. 

 12. On such submission we have gone through the averment of the application and the contention of both the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the parties. Since the petitioners have apparently failed to produce any documentary evidence in support of their title we find locus-standi even to challenge the authority of the respondent No. 1 to lease out the same as khas land which is alleged to be the product of accretion. Moreover, when it is admitted that once the petitioners filed a petition for lease they have no right to claim their own title by filling a photo copy of the kabala deed Annexure-B to the petition alleged to have been executed by one Salimullah in the year 1978. Even the deed does not bear any reference how the executants became the owner of the sea bed as described in the schedule.
